newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens weaker after selling in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens weaker after selling in Asia.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened slightly weaker on Monday at C$1.3792 (US$0.7251) from yesterday's close at C$1.3778 (US$0.7258). * The currency came under pressure after investors sold the unit overnight against the yen. * Traders said the currency could will begin triggering stop loss selling if it trades past C$1.38 (US$0.7246).

The weakness in Asia follows a session which saw the Canadian dollar come under pressure from a drop in the price of gold and gold stocks. The bullion price on Monday fell to its lowest level in 12 years.

Dealers said stop losses were in place on the Canadian dollar at C$1.3810 (US$0.7241) and the 100-day moving average was C$1.3808 (US$0.7242). Further weakness past these levels would trigger selling in the currency, dealers said.
"We'll be looking at some of those levels," the dealer said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dipped to 81.65 Japanese yen from 81.86 yen at Monday's close. The dollar firmed to 1.2740 German marks from 1.2717 marks on Monday.
